Sections.Title: Fall Armyworm
Sections.Scientific Name: Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith, 1797) | Order: Lepidoptera | F
Importance Notes: Invasive to India since 2018; now present in all Karnataka maize-growing districts.
A single larva can destroy an entire whorl in 24-48 hours at L4-L6 stage.
One adult female deposits 1,000-2,000 eggs; moths fly 100 km/night - rapid spread.
Karnataka losses documented at 25-73% in unmanaged fields (ICAR 2019-2023).
No natural immunity in existing Indian hybrids chemical & biological management is mandatory.

In soil 2-8 cm deep; last instar spins loose cocoon

Table.Colour / Appearance: Male: brown-grey wings with white patches; Female: dull uniform
Table.Key ID Feature: Male hindwings white; female hindwings pale grey; nocturnal

Table.Behaviour / Notes: Laid on leaf surface, covered with body scales; hatching synchronised

Long-distance migrant; lays eggs on maize, sorghum, sugarcane, wheat
No diapause continuous breeding; Kharif peak = Aug-Sep

Sections.Title: Stem Borer (Spotted Stalk Borer)
Sections.Scientific Name: Chilo partellus (Swinhoe, 1884) | Order: Lepidoptera | Family: Cra
Importance Notes: Chilo partellus is the primary stem borer of maize and sorghum in peninsular India.
Pre-dates FAW; co-exists with FAW after 2018 - dual infestation possible.
Causes 10-30% yield loss in unmanaged Kharif crops in Dharwad district.
Distinguished from FAW by regular shot-hole pattern and absence of frass in whorl.

Table.Key ID Feature: Laid in masses of 10-80 eggs on underside of leaf near midrib
Brown head; 4 brownish spots per segment (faint in L1)
4 distinct brownish spots on each abdominal segment; narrow body
Inside stem tunnel; cremaster with 8 hooked setae
Forewings with row of black dots; hindwings white; females larger

Table.Key Behaviour: Female lays 100-300 eggs/lifetime; prefers V3-V8 whorl leaves
Initially feed on surface; L2-L3 migrate to whorl and enter plant
Bore through stem; tunnel downward; cause Dead Heart / lodging
Pupate in feeding chamber; exit hole chewed before pupation
Nocturnal; attracted to lights; female needs protein meal before oviposition
Overlapping generations; peak damage in whorl stage Aug-Oct

Sections.Title: Shoot Fly
Sections.Scientific Name: Atherigona soccata / A. naqvii (Rondani) | Order: Diptera | Family.
Importance Notes: Shoot fly is exclusively a seedling pest - damage window is strictly 0-25 DAS.
After the 5-leaf stage (>25 DAS), plants become tolerant and shoot fly is no longer a threat.
In Kharif Dharwad, shoot fly incidence peaks during July-August on early-sown crops.
Yield loss of 20-35% possible in high-pressure fields with no seed treatment.

Sections.Title: Insecticide Resistance Management - Spray Rotation Guide

Subsections.Heading: RESISTANCE WARNING - KARNATAKA 2024
Points: FAW populations in Davangere and Dharwad have shown reduced sensitivity to Spinosad (Group 5).
Chlorpyrifos resistance confirmed in FAW populations in at least 3 Karnataka districts.
Resistance develops rapidly a single season of same-molecule use can select resistant biotypes.
Rotate MoA groups per spray; never apply same molecule more than TWICE per season.

Notes: Sprays 4 and 5 only if pheromone trap count remains above threshold after Spray 3.
Never apply two Group 28 (diamide) molecules in consecutive sprays even if products differ.
